# Format Bank (F1–F35), Modifiers, and Word Banks

Every format below is proven by view data (see `reference-titles.md` for sources and numbers). Generate by pairing these formats with proven topics. Do not invent new formats — extend this bank only from new winning data.

## Table of contents
1. Formats F1–F11 (proven on the user's own channel — highest confidence)
2. Formats F12–F35 (proven on audience-overlap/competitor channels)
3. Modifier families (attach to any format)
4. Word banks (power words, exclusivity ladder, adversaries, money language)
5. Structure skeletons (mirror these shapes)

---

## 1. Formats proven on the user's own channel (F1–F11)

- **F1 — The NEVER warning.** "X Things You Should NEVER Pour Down Your Drain" (1M views, 31x). Prohibition + implied disaster. Works as pure single clause.
- **F2 — Veteran authority / persona prevention.** "In 45 Years of Plumbing, I've Never Had a Clogged Drain — Here's Exactly What I Do" (444k). Credibility claimed in voiceover; perfect for faceless. The prevention-routine angle ("I've never had X — here's my routine") is its own lane distinct from fix-it content.
- **F3 — Numbered SECRETS + THOUSANDS.** "15 Plumbing SECRETS That Will Save You THOUSANDS!" (223k). Infinitely repeatable listicle engine; escalate the number over time (15 → 20 → 30).
- **F4 — Insider betrayal.** "…The Real Cause No Plumber Will Tell You" / "Methods Plumbers Don't Want You to Know" / "The PRO SECRET Nobody Teaches". Positions the persona as the honest insider breaking ranks.
- **F5 — Universal claim.** "Unclog ANY Toilet", "Destroys ANY Clog", "Works Every Single Time". Also the footage cheat code: universal methods justify generic compiled b-roll.
- **F6 — Ego challenge.** "I BET You Don't Know How to Use a Plunger Correctly — Most People Get This Wrong" (150k). Confrontational knowledge-gap hook.
- **F7 — Versus + test.** "SharkBite vs Solder — Which Is ACTUALLY Stronger! (Pressure Test!)". Product-debate content; the audience already has tribal opinions. 3-way escalation proven ("vs X vs Y — ALL 3").
- **F7b — Naked decision versus.** "Tankless vs Tank Water Heater" (269k, 18x multiplier with zero power words). High-intent purchase-moment queries need no hype and monetize better. Do not over-decorate these.
- **F8 — Pre-purchase gate.** "Watch This Video BEFORE Buying SHARKBITE Fittings (Everything You Need To Know)".
- **F9 — Failure prophecy.** "5 Reasons Your PEX Plumbing Will FAIL Within 5 Years — And How to Prevent a DISASTER!" / "8 FATAL MISTAKES…". Fear + stakes; "mistakes" listicles outperform straight tutorials.
- **F10 — Diagnostic.** "Why Your Toilet Keeps Clogging — The Real Cause…". Why-your-X-does-Y. Pairs naturally with F4 suffix.
- **F11 — Qualified how-to.** "…The RIGHT Way", "From SCRATCH", "Without It Dripping", "(Beginner's Guide)".

## 2. Formats proven on audience-overlap channels (F12–F35)

- **F12 — Effort minimization.** "A Ridiculously Easy Way to X" / "An Insanely Easy Way to X" (5.4M windshield video). Promises ease, not correction — friendlier trigger than "you're doing it wrong". Needs a job people currently believe is hard.
- **F13 — Cost substitution.** "X Is Expensive. Do This Instead!" (943k). Skip the paid service entirely. Plumbing services with DIY substitutes: drain cleaning, hydro jetting, heater flushes, leak detection.
- **F14 — Regret of ignorance.** "Hacks You'll Wish You Knew Sooner" (1.3M). Sympathetic sibling of F6 — same gap, warmer tone.
- **F15 — Scarcity alternatives.** "When You Can't Find X, Try These 3 Alternatives". Situational emergency + listicle ("without a plunger", "before the store opens").
- **F16 — Concrete benchmark.** "SEAL TIGHT as a Fridge". A vivid physical standard instead of an adjective.
- **F17 — Problem-question opener.** "Black Mold in Toilet Tank?" / "Rotten Egg Smell in Your Sink?" / "Toilet Keeps Running?". Opens by naming the viewer's exact problem as a question — instant self-selection. Meta-proven across 3+ channels. Title in the viewer's **sensory vocabulary** (what it sounds/smells/looks like), not the technical cause.
- **F18 — Quantified micro-solution.** "Remove It in 10 Minutes With This $3 No-Scrub Trick" (553k). Tiny time + tiny cost; specific constraints make the mystery credible. Extreme end proven: "in 60 Seconds".
- **F19 — Lost wisdom / suppression.** "BURIED Since 1947", "The Paint Industry Prayed You'd Never Find This", "Grandpa's 25 BANNED Borax Hacks from the '60s". For this channel, run the honest version: the persona IS the old-timer — "The Trick Plumbers Used Before Drain Cleaner Existed". Multi-channel proven (clones pull 200k–971k).
- **F20 — Causal horror diagnosis.** "Your Kitchen Drain Smells Because 10 Years of Grease Is Rotting Inside Your Pipes. $1 Crystal Ends It" (238k). Symptom → disgusting hidden cause with a time dimension → micro-cost cure. A complete story in one title.
- **F21 — The banned explainer.** "The REAL Reason S-Traps Are No Longer ALLOWED In Any Home!" (411k vs the user's plain explainer on the same topic — ~6–8x uplift from framing alone). Every dry code rule is a hidden scandal: saddle valves, polybutylene, galvanized, lead, Orangeburg. Needs a real rule.
- **F22 — The in-group secret.** "Why Don't Bugs Enter THEIR Homes? The $1 Secret They Put In Every Doorway". Third-person F2: "Why Plumbers' Own Drains Never Clog — The $2 Monthly Habit…". High confidence.
- **F23 — Mechanism mystery.** "Two Cheap Metals Eliminate ANY Bug Forever" (971k), "One Copper Cable…". Counted-but-unnamed components; "which two?" is a stronger itch than a named substance. Small numbers exempt from the listicle-length rule.
- **F24 — "…And Watch What Happens."** "Pour Hydrogen Peroxide into Your Toilet Tank and Watch What Happens" (1.8M in 9 months). The inverted tease: gives the method, hides the outcome. "Tonight" upgrade available.
- **F25 — N uses compendium.** "16 Uses for WD-40 Everyone Should Know" (5.7M). Substance as protagonist, breadth promise. Current meta prefers substance × specific fixture over generic "N uses" — see reference-titles for the evidence.
- **F26 — Never throw away X.** "You Will Never Throw Away Eggshells After Watching This" (4.4M). Behavior-change prophecy; weakest plumbing transfer — vocabulary more than a target.
- **F27 — Like never before / performance restoration.** "Unbelievable Trick to Make Your Toilet Flush Like Never Before!" (4.2M outlier on a faced channel). Enhancement framing — the fixture works but could be better than ever. The unserved middle between "broken" and "fine": flush power, water pressure, shower flow, drain speed.
- **F28 — Survivor shortlist.** "The Only 2 Water Heater Brands Still Built to Last" (118k). Extreme-filter buying guide riding the quality-decline narrative. "Only N" stays small — scarcity is the hook. Variant: "X EVERYONE IGNORES (But These N…)" — the overlooked gem.
- **F29 — The grade lie / quality exposé.** "Why 90% of New Home Plumbing Is Already Failing (The Builder Grade Lie)". Statistical doom + present-progressive decay + a named industry deception. Honest ammunition exists: big-box vs supply-house internals are documented fact.
- **F30 — Hidden asset reframe.** "Why Buy A Generator? You Have One Parked In Your Driveway." (2.3M). You already own the solution in disguise: the shop vac as drain tool, the water heater as 50 gallons of emergency water.
- **F31 — Family protection emergency.** "This $16 Hack Could Keep Your Family Warm During A Power Outage!" (744k). Provider identity + micro-cost + crisis: burst pipes, frozen pipes, the main shutoff, washer hoses, sump failure.
- **F32 — The truth about X.** "The Truth About Lawnmower Blade Sharpening: Test Results Exposed!" (1.8M). Myth-busting; honest-fit targets: flushable wipes, liquid drain cleaners, vinegar+baking soda.
- **F33 — STOP doing the default.** "Stop Spraying Wasp Nests — This Is The Trick Exterminators Don't Want You…" (194k in one week). NEVER prohibits; STOP commands cessation of the current behavior, then substitutes: "Stop Buying Drano —", "Stop Calling Roto-Rooter —".
- **F34 — Precise savings opener.** "Save $400 — What Plumbers Don't Want You to Know" (221k). Exact dollar figure first; the specific mid-size number is the credibility sweet spot between THOUSANDS and $1.
- **F35 — The recurrence problem.** "Why Does THIS Keep Coming Back and How to STOP It" (6.8M, durable pool). Chronic problems: the pink ring, the clog that returns, the smell that returns. "THIS" enables title-thumbnail interlock.

## 3. Modifier families (attach to any format)

- **Parentheticals** — use the flavor that kills the viewer's specific doubt:
  - Objection-killer: "(NO Haze or Streaks)", "(No Scrubbing)", "(No Parts Needed)"
  - Adversary tag: "(Dealers Hate This)", "(Plumbers Never Mention It)"
  - Credibility tag: "(Pro Tips)", "(Beginner's Guide)", "(45 Years of Pro Tips!)"
  - Surprise tease: "(The Results Will SURPRISE You!)", "(The Answer Will Surprise You!)"
  - Insider-term/loophole: "(The 'Commercial Grade' Loophole)", "(The Builder Grade Lie)", "(The Supply House Secret)" — teaching the trade's vocabulary is itself a hook
  - Guilt hook: "(You Use Most of Them Daily)", "(You're Probably Doing It)"
- **Urgency:** Tonight, RIGHT NOW, Before Tonight, This Weekend, Before You Ever Need It, Before Winter/Summer.
- **Totality/whole-house:** Every Drain in Your House, EVERY fixture, Completely, ALL.
- **Permanence/certainty:** FOREVER, PERMANENTLY, Permanent Fix, GUARANTEED, Ends It.
- **Effort negation (stackable):** No-Scrub, No Plunger, No Snake, No Tools, No Mess, No Chemicals, No Plumber, No Crawling. Staccato fragment delivery proven: "No Chemicals. No Plumber."
- **Safety reassurance:** Septic-Safe, Won't Damage Pipes, No Chemicals, Honey-Bee-Safe-style ethics tags, "Safe for Seniors" (test carefully — lands as targeted or patronizing).
- **Named-retailer anchor:** "The $2 Walmart Bag…", "The $4 Home Depot Part…" — folksy ultra-concreteness.
- **Present-progressive loss:** "That ARE Costing You", "Is Already FAILING", "Quietly Costing You" — money bleeding now, not hypothetically.
- **Title-thumbnail interlock:** "THIS" in the title forces the thumbnail to complete the meaning; neither spoils alone.

## 4. Word banks

- **Caps-worthy power words:** NEVER, STOP, SECRETS, GENIUS, THOUSANDS, FREE, GUARANTEED, FOREVER, PERMANENTLY, ANY, ALL, EVERY, FATAL, BANNED, ILLEGAL, REAL, TRUTH, ACTUALLY, RIGHT NOW, BET, WRONG, DESTROY, SEVERELY, ULTIMATE, HOT, OWN.
- **Lost-wisdom vocabulary:** Grandpa's, old plumbers, old-school, Ancient, before X existed, from the '60s, still unbeaten, swore by.
- **Exclusivity ladder (climb as needed):** Most people get this wrong → Plumbers don't want you to know → Nobody teaches → NO ONE knows about → The industry pretends it doesn't exist.
- **Adversary roster:** plumbers (as a trade — the persona is the exception), Roto-Rooter, the water company, big-box stores, builders ("builder grade"), brand manufacturers, "the industry".
- **Money language by scale:** FREE (terminal point — beats cheap for this audience) → 50¢ / $1 / $2 / $3 / $5 (micro-cost, makes the trick concrete) → Save $400-style exact figures (credibility sweet spot) → THOUSANDS (vague-big stakes). Use one scale per title.
- **Disgust vocabulary:** gunk, grease, grime, sludge, slime, rotting, biofilm, sewage, black gunk. A click emotion plumbing is rich in.
- **Sensory symptom words (title in the viewer's own words):** banging, gurgling, rotten egg smell, sagging, hissing, weak, slow, keeps coming back.

## 5. Structure skeletons (mirror these shapes; vary across a batch)

- Single clause listicle: "7 Things You Should NEVER Flush Down Your Toilet"
- Listicle + payoff: "15 GENIUS Vinegar Tricks That Will Save Your Plumbing THOUSANDS!"
- Persona two-part: "In 45 Years of Plumbing, I've Never [X] — Here's Exactly What I [Do/Use]"
- Question opener + fix: "Toilet Keeps Running? The FREE 5-Minute Fix (No Parts Needed)"
- Diagnostic two-part: "Why Your [X] Keeps [Y] — The Real Cause No Plumber Will Tell You"
- Action tease: "Pour [substance] Into Your [fixture] Tonight and Watch What Happens"
- Causal horror: "Your [X] [symptom] Because [hidden cause] — This $[1-5] [fix] Ends It"
- Versus: "[A] vs [B] — Which One ACTUALLY [outcome]?" (naked version allowed: "[A] vs [B] [category]")
- Shortlist: "The Only [2-3] [products] [pros] Actually Trust (Everything Else [fails])"
- STOP substitution: "STOP [default behavior] — The $[X] Trick [insiders] Have Quietly Used for [time]"
- Banned story: "The REAL Reason [X] Was BANNED [scope]!"
- Challenge: "I BET You [don't know / are doing X wrong] — [Most People Get This Wrong / N Mistakes]"
